🚨🇲🇽 <u>"One flag, one people, one homeland"</u>

Sheinbaum says once state congresses ratify the reform barring dual nationals from the presidency, governorships and Mexico City's top office, it takes effect immediately. She added that Morena must explain naming US-born Jasmine Bugarín as its Nayarit coordinator. Candidates, she said, need "one flag, one people, one homeland."

Two days later, Bugarín was at the US consulate in Guadalajara starting the paperwork to renounce her US citizenship: "Mexico is my homeland."

The rule applied to Morena first.

text:
🇲🇽🏭 <u>Health tenders: Mexican suppliers' volume up 301%</u>

Mexico's Health Secretariat closed its 2027-2028 medical-supplies tender: 12.569 billion pesos for 646 million pieces, 94.5% of the volume requested.

The story is who's making them. Codes awarded to Mexican industry jumped from 90 to 173 (+92%), and pieces from 148 million to 594.6 million, a 301% increase.

In 2019, La Jornada reported that just ten companies had concentrated the health sector's medicine purchases under the previous government. Now public money is buying national production.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>FDA closes the case: no proof Mexican produce caused the outbreaks</u>

Mexico's health regulator Cofepris says the FDA closed its Salmonella Javiana and Cyclospora investigations on October 2 without analytical evidence that Mexican products were the source. On Salmonella, every sample came back negative and the FDA couldn't identify a route or source of contamination. On Cyclospora, it found two positive environmental samples (wastewater and a drainage ditch), yet Cofepris's own lab tests on raw material, finished product and plant water were all negative.

Same produce panic Washington used in July to wave tariffs at Mexican lettuce. Cofepris: "Any conclusion on the origin of a health risk must be backed by verifiable, conclusive scientific evidence."
banner: FDA: NO PROOF MEXICAN PRODUCE TO BLAME

text:
🇲🇽🍽️ <u>Fewer Mexican Households Going Hungry: 19.5% → 11.5% in a Decade</u>

INEGI's 2025 Intercensal Survey, reported by El Economista: in 2015, 19.45% of Mexican households said an adult had eaten less than they needed for lack of money. In 2025 that figure was 11.50%. Households where an adult skipped a meal fell from 10.72% to 7.13%.

The drivers are on the record. The share of households receiving income from social programs rose from 25% in 2020 to 41.4% in 2025, and the monthly minimum wage went from 2,800 pesos in 2018 to 9,584 pesos in 2026.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>An Austrian Presidential Hopeful Promises to Send Moctezuma's Headdress Home</u>

Economist Günther Fehlinger-Jahn, who is running for Austria's 2028 presidency, pledged to officially return the Penacho de Moctezuma to Mexico if he wins. He called the feathered headdress a symbol of the colonial past and said returning cultural property to its countries of origin would be a foreign-policy priority.

The Penacho has been in Austria since 1596 and now sits in Vienna's ethnographic museum. Vienna still refuses Mexico's requests, citing more than 170 fractures that it says make transport impossible.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Cerimedo's Network Runs Through the PRI and Claudio X's Sí por México</u>

A new Contralínea investigation traces Fernando Cerimedo's Miami-based disinformation network into Mexico's opposition: the PRI leadership and Sí por México, the platform bankrolled by Kimberly-Clark shareholder Claudio X. González that backed Xóchitl Gálvez.

The thread also reaches Alonso Cedeño, who shares stages with Dick Morris, "the mind behind the slogan 'López Obrador is a danger to Mexico'" in 2006. Cerimedo, Milei's former adviser and co-owner of La Derecha Diario, now faces prosecution in Bolivia for attempted femicide and money laundering.
banner: CERIMEDO NETWORK REACHES PRI, CLAUDIO X

text:
🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>Havana Salutes Morena at 15</u>

Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel congratulated Mexico's governing party on its 15th anniversary: "Our sincere congratulations to Morena for the 15 years of its foundation. We reiterate from the Communist Party of Cuba the commitment to continue deepening the ties of friendship and cooperation between our political organizations."

Morena was founded as a civil association on October 2, 2011, the anniversary of Tlatelolco, and won registration as a national party in 2014. Fifteen years later it governs Mexico, while Washington tightens the blockade on the island.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Operación Enjambre Hits Chiapas: Morena Mayor and Ex-Mayor Arrested</u>

Mexico's federal anti-corruption sweep just took down its own party's people. At 5:30 a.m. Saturday, federal forces arrested Suchiapa mayor Jorge Lara Cordero and former mayor Alexis Nucamendi, both from Morena, along with 19 others, including municipal police commanders and judicial staff.

The Security Cabinet says all 21 are under investigation for abuse of authority, corruption and criminal association. The raid comes days after the town's police director was detained over a prisoner's escape.

🇲🇽✊ "For thirty-six years they said that if the minimum wage went up there would be inflation… Between President López Obrador and us, the minimum wage has gone up 154 percent in real terms." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Vivienda para el Bienestar, Tejería, Veracruz The minimum wage was 2,800 pesos a month in 2018. Today it is more than 9,500. The Constitution now requires every government to raise it above the previous year's inflation. Higher wages also capitalized Infonavit and IMSS, which receive a share of payroll, and that money now funds 1.2 million homes this term and new hospital beds.

Nothing." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Vivienda para el Bienestar, Tejería, Veracruz Leobardo had borrowed 67,000 pesos from Infonavit. Infonavit found 4,856,000 "unpayable" loans issued under neoliberal governments, whose balances grew even as borrowers kept paying. All of them have now been restructured, 200,000 of them in Veracruz. Another 150,000 paid-off Veracruz mortgages are being released free of charge. The registry procedure used to cost 16,000 to 18,000 pesos.
